# Decisions

Rules that span modules, from each package's `Decisions:`. Owner rules end with `(owner)`.

## Owner

- `authorlm.audio`: Export resolves explicitly configured per-paragraph voices from the manuscript's `_audio/audiobook.toml` and cast into the shared manifest; both consumers use those resolved parameters. Enforced by: tests/test_audio_voice_config.py::VoiceConfigTests::test_required_voice_fields_are_not_filled_in and tests/test_audio_voice_config.py::VoiceConfigTests::test_chapter_override_is_exact_file_without_inheritance. (owner)
- `authorlm.audio`: Mac say previews and export do not require an ElevenLabs Voice ID; paid synthesis does. Explicit cast roles remain required. Enforced by tests/test_audio_preview_without_paid_voice.py. (owner)
- `authorlm.devedit`: A letter is written at the end of each stage, over every stage so far (never the stages still to come), and judges what that much of the book delivers against what it promises, maps every concept as introduced, asserted, demonstrated or assumed, and lists at most ten problems, each with evidence, why it matters, a remedy and its dependencies. (owner)
- `authorlm.devedit`: Coverage comes from `toc.toml` and is confirmed by the author before any step runs; only files the TOC lists are covered, and `outside` files never are. (owner)
- `authorlm.devedit`: Each letter decision is binding or provisional; a later step may raise a provisional one for reconsideration, never override either. (owner)
- `authorlm.devedit`: Run state lives in the manuscript folder, `_devedit/<run-id>/`, beside `_critiques`, and travels with the manuscript. (owner)
- `authorlm.devedit`: Strengths the letter names are preserved, not frozen: a later step may move a strong passage or add a transition, never weaken what makes it strong. (owner)
- `authorlm.devedit`: The integrator reads every proposed item together after the essay agents, from a deterministic grouping by term, concept, dependency and paragraph, and makes the items mutually consistent. (owner)
- `authorlm.gdocs`: A tab's anchor in the whole-Doc export is its opening heading (level and text), the split backs up over any epigraph paragraphs before it, and opening headings must be unique across tabs and must not recur as a heading in an earlier tab; the pull stops and names the pair otherwise. Why: first-paragraph anchors let a short dialogue line ("Yes.") steal the prior chapter's tail; a uniqueness gate over the whole export dropped tabs whose opener is echoed later. Enforced by: tests/test_anchor_split_and_holds.py::test_dialogue_line_is_not_an_anchor, tests/test_anchor_split_and_holds.py::test_epigraph_lands_in_its_own_tab, tests/test_anchor_split_and_holds.py::test_duplicate_opening_heading_stops_the_pull, tests/test_anchor_split_and_holds.py::test_opening_heading_inside_an_earlier_tab_stops_the_pull, tests/test_anchor_split_and_holds.py::test_tab_without_heading_stops_the_pull. (owner)
- `authorlm.terms`: Extraction and the developmental edit share this one implementation of the term rules, so the two cannot drift apart. (owner)
- `authorlm.terms`: The term index is built from the manuscript text alone, fresh on every call; nothing in the concept graph or `_concepts` notes is treated as authoritative. (owner)

## Agent-drafted

- `authorlm.book`: A restart never supersedes a wider scope: a part or book step already done on the old work stays done and is flagged on the board as resting on a restarted step, for the author to decide. Enforced by: tests/test_book_workflow.py::RestartTests::test_a_wider_step_that_rested_on_a_restarted_one_is_flagged.
- `authorlm.book`: Any step can be restarted, for any reason (wrong information from the author, a flawed prompt, missing context). What that step and the steps that followed it produced, for the same scope and the scopes inside it, is kept and marked superseded; the rerun is handed the old result as reference only, with no authority over the new one. What was made before never becomes the standard. Enforced by: tests/test_book_workflow.py::RestartTests::test_restart_supersedes_the_step_and_its_dependents_only and tests/test_book_workflow.py::RestartTests::test_the_rerun_is_handed_the_old_result_as_reference_only.
- `authorlm.book`: Between agent steps nothing stops: a step is ready as soon as every step it follows is done for its scope. When a step's actor is a person the run waits, the board says who is waited on, and that person is notified. Enforced by: tests/test_book_workflow.py::OrderingTests::test_the_book_runs_in_order_across_all_three_grains and tests/test_book_workflow.py::HumanStepTests::test_a_human_step_waits_names_the_person_and_notifies.
- `authorlm.book`: Each agent role may have a role file in the checkout, `.claude/agents/book-<role slug>.md`: a Claude Code subagent that says how that trade does its step with AuthorLM's existing verbs. When one exists, an agent step's pack names it near the top, so whoever starts the step knows which subagent to hand it to. The role file is advice on method; the contract in the pack is the one in force. A missing role file, or a package installed outside a checkout, changes nothing else. Enforced by: tests/test_book_role_agents.py::PackNamesTheRoleFileTests::test_an_agent_steps_pack_names_its_role_file and tests/test_book_role_agents.py::PackNamesTheRoleFileTests::test_a_role_without_a_file_gets_a_pack_that_names_none.
- `authorlm.book`: Each step names its actor, `agent` or `human:<who>`, and the actor can be changed per book and per step (`assign`) without touching anything else: a person and an agent are interchangeable holders of a role. A run copies the actor when it starts, so a later change never rewrites what happened. Enforced by: tests/test_book_workflow.py::AssignTests::test_assign_swaps_the_actor_and_old_runs_keep_theirs.
- `authorlm.book`: Every change of a run's status is one row of `step_events`, written in the same transaction by the one function that changes a status (`_transition`); the table is only ever appended to, so it is the record of what happened and when (`history`). Enforced by: tests/test_book_workflow.py::HistoryTests::test_no_run_has_a_status_its_last_event_does_not_give and tests/test_book_workflow.py::HistoryTests::test_only_one_function_writes_a_runs_status.
- `authorlm.book`: Every pack carries the register entries in scope, with the author's words and the machine's reading (register.py), and tells the role to record a use, `applies` or `infers`, for each entry its work rests on. Enforced by: tests/test_book_workflow.py::PackTests::test_the_pack_carries_the_register_in_scope.
- `authorlm.book`: No walls: a pack lists what a role is handed up front and never limits what it may read; any role may read the whole manuscript. The one exception is declared per step: an `independent` reader is not handed what the steps before it returned, nor its own earlier attempt. Enforced by: tests/test_book_workflow.py::PackTests::test_the_pack_states_the_contract and tests/test_book_workflow.py::PackTests::test_an_independent_step_is_not_handed_earlier_outputs.
- `authorlm.book`: Recording what rested on the register is not left to the role's memory: an agent's run of a step that is given the register is marked done only when its result declares its uses (`register_uses`), each labelled applies or infers, or says it rested on none and why. `done` writes those uses under the run, through `register.use`. A person's step is exempt. Why: the author must be able to tell a choice they made from one made for them. Enforced by: tests/test_book_workflow.py::RegisterUsesOnDoneTests::test_done_is_declined_without_the_key_and_names_it and tests/test_book_workflow.py::RegisterUsesOnDoneTests::test_the_uses_are_written_under_the_run.
- `authorlm.book`: The definition may change while a book is in flight. Steps are matched by their id, never by position, and each run records a fingerprint of the definition file and of its step's contract as they were when it started; the board says when a run in force was made under an earlier version of its step's contract. Enforced by: tests/test_book_workflow.py::DefinitionVersionTests::test_steps_are_matched_by_id_not_by_position and tests/test_book_workflow.py::DefinitionVersionTests::test_status_says_when_a_run_was_made_under_an_earlier_contract.
- `authorlm.book`: The diagram (`diagram`) is drawn from the definition file and the runs each time it is asked for, as Mermaid flowchart text and as its nodes and edges; nothing here renders it. A step's state has one source (`_cell`) for the status board and the diagram, so the two cannot disagree; superseded is a run's status and never a step's state. Enforced by: tests/test_book_workflow.py::DiagramTests::test_adding_a_step_changes_the_diagram and tests/test_book_workflow.py::DiagramTests::test_every_node_carries_the_state_the_status_board_gives.
- `authorlm.book`: The trade's order is large to small, and each role's contract (`leaves_alone`) says what it does not change: a later role that finds an earlier-level problem files it back and does not fix it.
- `authorlm.book`: The workflow is sequential steps, `after` dependencies, one run per scope of a step's grain, and supersede. It has no gateways, timers or conditions.
- `authorlm.devedit`: A verdict applies the item to the manuscript file only if the original text is still there exactly once; otherwise the item is stale and is checked again. Enforced by: tests/test_devedit.py::test_apply_refuses_changed_text.
- `authorlm.devedit`: An essay agent is given its essay's essay, section and paragraph summaries, the essay summaries of the essays already edited (later ones by title only), and the terms the edited essays established; it fetches anything else through authorlm verbs. (owner, 2026-11-09)
- `authorlm.devedit`: Essays are edited one at a time in reading order. One essay's pass is: findings, checks, the author's review, the accepted items applied, its summary rebuilt, then a notebook entry (`note`); the next essay's pack is refused until then (`--trial` excepted). The notebook is the shared memory: each agent's reasoning and the author's feedback, condensed on purpose, readable and correctable by the author. (owner, 2026-11-09)
- `authorlm.devedit`: Every agent works within the standing context: the file's style law (prose aspects only), the audience and market profiles and the example-arcs list; it reads manuscript text only through `read`, which serves covered files alone (author ruling 2026-11-09: nothing outside the final manuscript); the structural style law binds the proposals, sentence-level law waits for the line edit. Essay agents run one at a time in reading order, each given the arcs the earlier agents proposed. (owner, 2026-11-09)
- `authorlm.devedit`: Items are tiered must, should and could, with no cap. Every item is shown with a short reason (`why`, five to ten words); the full reason, the finding and the checker's note come when the author asks. (owner, 2026-11-09, replacing "the reason only when asked")
- `authorlm.devedit`: Nothing in authorlm's stored notes is authoritative: an essay's summary is rebuilt at the start of its pass and again after its items are applied, never the whole book up front; the term index is computed from the text. (owner, 2026-11-09)
- `authorlm.devedit`: The queue and the verdicts live in the workspace database beside `doc_threads`, written per row in transactions, safe for several agents at once; the documents stay files. (owner, 2026-11-13)
- `authorlm.devedit`: The term index grows with the edit: it is computed from the finished essays only, never the current or later ones. (owner, 2026-11-09)
- `authorlm.devedit`: Within a run the standard holds still: the ledger records every finding as addressed, declined, dropped or open; a rerun or a letter closes what was addressed and never reverses, re-raises or raises the bar on a closed finding. A new run starts with an empty ledger. (owner, 2026-11-09)
- `authorlm.docs`: A chapter has a stable identifier independent of the name the author sees, so it can be renamed cheaply: no record is lost or orphaned by a rename. Enforced by: tests/test_document_identity.py::RenameVerbTests::test_rename_carries_every_record_to_the_new_name and tests/test_document_identity.py::RenameOnDiskTests::test_a_rename_on_disk_heals_at_the_next_collect.
- `authorlm.docs`: An existing manuscript is untouched until its owner turns document ids on, after a backup: with the setting off a collect behaves as it did before documents had ids. Enforced by: tests/test_document_identity.py::DocumentIdsSwitchTests::test_off_a_rename_on_disk_collects_exactly_as_it_did_before and tests/test_document_identity.py::DocumentIdsSwitchTests::test_turning_it_on_backs_up_first_then_seeds_every_file.
- `authorlm.docs`: `doc rename` is declined while the file is checked out to Google Docs, has a live filter run, a writeup in flight or pending forms: each holds state tied to the name while it runs. A rename made outside AuthorLM in one of those states cannot be declined and is carried all the same. Enforced by: tests/test_document_identity.py::RenameDeclinedTests.
- `authorlm.register`: A key is unique among the live entries (proposed, settled, reopened) of its kind in a manuscript, kept here in code, never by a unique index. Enforced by: tests/test_register.py::KeyTests::test_a_key_is_unique_among_live_entries_of_its_kind.
- `authorlm.register`: An entry holds both the author's words, verbatim, and the machine's reading of them, and cannot be settled without both. Why: the machine's reading of a choice is not always the author's, and the author must be able to see the reading before work rests on it. Enforced by: tests/test_register.py::SettleTests::test_settling_needs_the_reading and tests/test_register.py::SettleTests::test_settling_needs_the_authors_words.
- `authorlm.register`: New words the machine has not read back are not settled: revising the author's words without a new reading leaves the new entry proposed. Enforced by: tests/test_register.py::ReviseAndReopenTests::test_new_words_without_a_new_reading_wait_for_the_author.
- `authorlm.register`: No approval is eternal: a settled entry can be reopened, and its words or reading can change. A change is never an edit in place: it makes a new entry that supersedes the old one, the old one stays readable, and the change returns every use of the old one, the work that now needs a look. Enforced by: tests/test_register.py::ReviseAndReopenTests::test_revising_a_settled_entry_supersedes_it_and_returns_its_uses and tests/test_register.py::ReviseAndReopenTests::test_reopening_returns_the_work_that_rested_on_the_entry.
- `authorlm.register`: Work rests only on a settled entry, and every piece of work that rests on one records a use that says whether it applies the entry as written or infers something the entry does not say. Why: the author must never be told "you told me to do this" about something they did not say. Enforced by: tests/test_register.py::UseTests::test_a_use_says_applies_or_infers_and_nothing_else and tests/test_register.py::UseTests::test_work_cannot_rest_on_an_entry_that_is_not_settled.
